key_insight: The paper replaces static CT image reconstruction with direct recovery of particle trajectories from radiographs, enabling much faster 3D X-ray particle tracking velocimetry in opaque porous media.
engineering_relevance: This advances pore-scale flow measurement for geo-energy, electrochemistry, and other applications where conventional CT-based velocimetry is too slow for fast-moving tracers.
method: Bypasses intermediate 3D CT volume reconstruction and links trajectories directly from radiographs.
Implements the approach in the open-source CTracks algorithm.
Validates performance on pipe flow and complex porous-media experiments, plus numerical simulations.
evidence_signal: Experiments and simulations show a five-fold increase in maximum detectable velocity, with improved detection rates and bounded trajectory errors.
watch_item: The approach still depends on radiograph quality and trajectory assignment robustness, so performance may degrade in very dense or highly ambiguous particle fields.
paper_title: Direct Trajectory Reconstruction for Fast 3D X-ray Particle Tracking Velocimetry in Porous Media
